**Strategy for catching every new community announcement the moment it’s posted**

1. **Follow the official announcement thread**  
   The forum’s announcement posts always start with a **TL;DR line** that instantly tells you what’s new — see the “TL;DR line” element in the *Forum Announcement Drafting* concept【concepts/forum-announcement-drafting.md】. By bookmarking that thread (or the forum’s “Announcements” sub‑forum) you can open it as soon as a new post appears.

2. **Enable real‑time notifications**  
   Most forum platforms let you “watch” a thread or a category. Turn on **push or email alerts** for the Announcements category so you receive a notification the instant a TL;DR line is posted.

3. **Use an RSS feed (if available)**  
   If the forum provides an RSS/Atom feed for the Announcements section, add it to your feed reader. The feed will deliver the **brief description** and the TL;DR instantly, letting you skim without opening the full page.

4. **Create a personal “quick‑scan” checklist**  
   - Open the new post → read the TL;DR line.  
   - Scan the **brief description** (3‑4 sentences) for the affected features.  
   - Click the **full‑announcement** and **changelog** links (they’re always on separate lines in the template).  
   This checklist mirrors the structure recommended in the *Forum Announcement Drafting* concept and lets you verify you haven’t missed anything.

5. **Leverage placeholder‑ready templates for your own follow‑up**  
   Keep a copy of the announcement template (with placeholders) in a personal note. When a new post arrives, you can quickly fill in the placeholders with the actual feature names, URLs, and any settings you need to check. This habit reinforces that you’ve read the announcement and helps you act on it immediately.

6. **Set a daily “announcement window”**  
   If the community tends to post at certain times (e.g., mornings), schedule a 5‑minute check‑in during that window. Because you already have the TL;DR line at the top, you’ll know instantly whether a new announcement dropped.

7. **Engage the community promptly**  
   The template includes an invitation to **reply with any issues**. By responding early, you stay visible in the conversation and can get clarification on any ambiguous points right away.

By combining **forum watching**, **notification feeds**, and the **structured TL;DR‑first format** that all official announcements follow, you’ll be able to spot and process every new announcement the instant it’s published.
